bug_semantics: _list_globals() walks backward from STACK_GLOBAL with for offset in range(1, n), which never inspects ops[0]. A pickle that places a STACK_GLOBAL argument at opcode index 0 therefore yields only one tracked argument, raises ValueError, and the scanner fails closed as a detection bypass. Invalid/malicious globals are not reported.
flaw_origin: First write of the STACK_GLOBAL backward scan in 18c978e9a298a2e08a040dc2ed9ee6413bc7c6c8 (Add support for multiple pickles per file). That commit replaced the prior ops[n-2]/ops[n-1] pair with for offset in range(1, n), omitting position 0. Later scanner commits kept that range until the fix; they did not introduce the off-by-one.
evidence: CVE-2025-71325 is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected); GHSA-9gvj-pp9x-gcfr withdrawn_at is null. Advisory describes STACK_GLOBAL argument tracking using the wrong loop range so a payload with the first arg at opcode 0 raises and bypasses detection. Direct fix 58983e1c20973ac42f2df7ff15d7c8cd32f9b688 (PR #46, parent 2974a252df7649ca910c4d6c79afa1029ee99423) changes range(1, n) to range(1, n + 1) on src/picklescan/scanner.py; pre-fix parent still has range(1, n) and raises ValueError when len(values) != 2. git log -S 'range(1, n)' on that path bottoms out at 18c978e9a298a2e08a040dc2ed9ee6413bc7c6c8. Parent 9c31e17959dab1893874235ade2a140d5553c8ef still has src/picklescan/scanner.py (cat-file -e succeeds) but STACK_GLOBAL uses ops[n-2]/ops[n-1] with no range(1, n).
